subject: DPA: keystore custody, legal hold & transfer requirements
body:
From: Claire Jones <claire.jones@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: keystore custody, legal hold & transfer requirements

Hi Michael / Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start legal review, a few must-haves from our side for any Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) engagement:

- Customer-controlled keys (BYOK) with support for HSM-backed keystores; explicit clause that Redwood will not have unilateral access to plaintext keys.
- Escrow arrangement: process for key escrow, how keys are stored, who can request restoration, and dual-authority controls.
- Operator access model: we need a non-service-account operator model; verification that Redwood operators cannot decrypt customer data and that any break-glass access is logged and requires two approvers.
- Legal hold & eDiscovery: process for export of data under legal hold, retention preservation, and proof of chain of custody for exports.
- Subprocessors & transfers: list of subprocessors, data transfer mechanisms for EU data (SCCs or equivalent), and commitments around geo-boundary enforcement.

I'm attaching our standard DPA (Acme_DPA_v2.docx) with redlines expected. Can you confirm these items are supported and, if so, provide proposed contract language or a redline back? Also please point me to any operational runbooks for the on-prem install that cover escrow and break-glass.

Goal: legal wants to finish review by EOD Wednesday (3/17).

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Jones
Director, Legal Operations
Acme Health Technologies

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Jones <claire.jones@acmehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc:

Subject: Re: DPA: keystore custody, legal hold & transfer requirements

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. High-level confirmation first, then attachments and next steps below.

- BYOK & HSM: Supported. Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) can be configured with customer-managed KMS keys (Cloud KMS / on-prem HSM). We also offer a customer-kept keystore where only the customer holds the plaintext key; Redwood can be configured to operate without access to key material.
- Escrow: We support an escrow process but it is opt-in. Escrow keys are encrypted and require dual-authority release (customer admin + Redwood legal/sre approvers or an external escrow agent). We will provide a proposal for escrow language — see attached RDW_DPA_redline_v1.docx for initial language.
- Operator access / break-glass: Redwood operators do not have default decryption rights. Break-glass access is an audited, time-limited process that requires two independent approvers and generates immutable audit entries (operator id, reason, artifacts exported).
- Legal hold & eDiscovery: We provide export tooling for tenant exports with manifest and SHA256 checksums to prove integrity. Exports preserve timestamps and include an audit trail showing who requested the export and when.
- Subprocessors & transfers: We will provide an up-to-date subprocessor list and can contractually commit to SCCs (EU) or an adequacy mechanism where applicable. For fully on-prem deployments inside customer-controlled networks, data egress is governed by the deployment config.

Attached: RDW_DPA_redline_v1.docx (initial redline), keystore_diagram.png (ops view). I pulled in Neha (solutions) to detail the operational flow and Lauren (privacy counsel) to review the contract language.

Proposed next steps:
1) Lauren reviews and suggests final DPA language (I can then route to Acme CISO)
2) Neha shares escrow/runbook excerpts for your legal ops review
3) We set a 30-minute call Wednesday 3/17 morning to resolve any open items and, if OK, circulate DocuSign link

Best,
Michael Grant

Claire — looping in quick comments on the redline and some specific contract language we should align on. See in-line below and summarized asks.

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 10:08 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Attached: RDW_DPA_redline_v1.docx (initial redline), keystore_diagram.png (ops view). I pulled in Neha (solutions) to detail the operational flow and Lauren (privacy counsel) to review the contract language.

Summary of legal asks from Redwood:
- Operator access: contractual statement that "Redwood personnel shall not have access to customer plaintext keys or decrypted customer data except, in narrow break-glass scenarios, as set out in the Escrow & Break-Glass Procedures annex." We will include a new Annex describing the approvals, retention of logs, and notification timelines.
- Escrow release: require dual-authorization (customer security officer + Redwood legal ops) OR release to an appointed third-party escrow agent. Redwood prefers an external escrow agent for stronger auditability — we can include that option in the annex.
- Subprocessors: commit to notify Acme 30 days before onboarding a new subprocessor and to provide a mechanism for reasonable objection; include a current list as an appendix.
- Transfers: for EU data we will adopt SCCs (2021) where applicable; if Acme requires a bespoke data transfer addendum, we can scope that as an SOW item.
- Legal hold: add an obligation to preserve export manifests and a 90-day hold-on-exports retention if litigation notice provided; outline chain-of-custody metadata fields required.

Neha — can you confirm the ops artifacts we will share (keystore diagram, example escrow runbook excerpt, and export manifest template)?

- Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Regulatory
Redwood Inference

Claire / team — technical ops detail below and attached runbook excerpt. Happy to walk through live.

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 02:36 PM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Neha — can you confirm the ops artifacts we will share (keystore diagram, example escrow runbook excerpt, and export manifest template)?

We will provide the following artifacts for an on-prem / VPC private deployment:
1) Keystore diagram (attached): shows key lifecycle when customer supplies KMS/HSM; indicates the points where Redwood services receive tokens rather than key material.
2) Escrow runbook excerpt (attached escrow_runbook_v1.pdf): describes how keys are encrypted for escrow, where they are stored (customer-managed encryption envelope), and the dual-authorization release flow. Release requests require: (a) a signed request from an Acme admin, (b) two Redwood approvers OR a third-party escrow agent's signed release. All releases generate an immutable audit bundle.
3) Break-glass process: documented step-by-step; requests open a ticket, SRE triage, legal approval, and an auditor-issued export that captures full provenance (requester, approver ids, timestamps, checksums).
4) eDiscovery export manifest: JSON manifest includes file hashes, export timestamp, requester id, and a signed manifest (we will provide template).
5) Subprocessor list & notification: we will provide a current list and a notification cadence; if Acme wants a contractual objection process we can include a reasonable objection clause.

Notes on transfers: if acme configures an on-prem deployment within EU-bound infrastructure with no outbound routing, there is no cross-border transfer. For hosted dedicated deployments, SCCs are the default transfer mechanism for processing EU personal data.

Attachments: keystore_diagram.png, escrow_runbook_v1.pdf

Let me know if you want a short ops walkthrough before Wed.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
